title: Retiring from the Virginia Retirement System: plan, eligibility, service credit and survivors
about: The Virginia Retirement System pilot as a question family (``fixtures/families/retirement_va.json``). Statuses: required = applies to you now; recommended = an option worth checking; ask first = depends on your employer's election; not required = not (yet) eligible.
inspiration: The idea of tagging inputs as published facts, assumptions or scenario values, personas and one-at-a-time sensitivity comes from github.com/dam8u/VRSLite (no licence: nothing copied).
status: Computed from grounded decision tables, not reviewed by a person; not legal or financial advice. VRS decides every benefit; its handbooks and the member's own record govern.

source.quote: "State employee" means any person who is regularly employed full time on a salaried basis, whose tenure is not restricted as to temporary or provisional appointment, in the service of, and whose compensation is payable, no more often than biweekly, in whole or in part, by the Commonwealth or any department, institution, or agency thereof.
"Teacher" means any person who is regularly employed full time on a salaried basis as a professional or clerical employee of a county, city, or other local public school board.

values.label: Political subdivision (county, city, town) general employee

source.quote: The governing body of a political subdivision may adopt a resolution requesting that its eligible employees become members of the retirement system.

values.label: Hazardous duty: state police, VaLORS, or a political subdivision's law-enforcement officer, firefighter or EMT with enhanced benefits

source.quote: By resolution legally adopted and approved by the Board, the employer may elect to provide benefits equivalent to those provided under the State Police Officers' Retirement System

dimensions.name: membership
dimensions.label: When you first became a VRS member

values.label: Before 1 July 2010, with 5 years of service by 1 January 2013

source.quote: Was hired or rehired before July 1, 2010. Has at least five years of service credit as of January 1, 2013. Has not taken a refund.

values.label: Before 1 July 2010, without 5 years of service by 1 January 2013

source.quote: However, for any (i) person who becomes a member on or after July 1, 2010, or (ii) member who does not have at least 60 months of creditable service as of January 1, 2013, under this chapter his normal retirement date shall be the date that the member attains his "retirement age" as defined under the Social Security Act
Was hired or rehired before July 1, 2010, and does not have at least five years of service credit as of January 1, 2013. Was hired or rehired from July 1, 2010, to December 31, 2013.

Every person who is otherwise eligible to participate in the program but is not a member of a retirement plan administered by the Virginia Retirement System the first time he is hired or rehired on or after January 1, 2014, in a covered position, shall participate in the hybrid retirement program established by this section.

values.label: On or after 1 January 2014 (hazardous duty: not in the hybrid program)

source.quote: or a person eligible to earn the benefits permitted by § 51.1-138 shall not be eligible to participate in the hybrid retirement program.

derived.name: plan
derived.label: VRS plan, determined by the membership date

constraints.text: Service cannot exceed working years: under 50 means fewer than 30 years
Members since 2014 have at most about 13 years of membership service, plus up to four purchased years (as of 2026)
A member vested by 1 January 2013 has at least 5 years of service

employer.label: Your employer's human resources office (the VRS employer)

rules.title: Check your plan: VRS Plan 1. Your normal retirement date is your 65th birthday

source.quote: "Normal retirement date" means a member's sixty-fifth birthday.

rules.title: Check your plan: VRS Plan 2. Your normal retirement date is your Social Security retirement age

source.quote: However, for any (i) person who becomes a member on or after July 1, 2010, or (ii) member who does not have at least 60 months of creditable service as of January 1, 2013, under this chapter his normal retirement date shall be the date that the member attains his "retirement age" as defined under the Social Security Act

rules.title: Check your plan: the VRS Hybrid Retirement Plan (a Plan 2 style defined benefit and a defined contribution part)

source.quote: Every person who is otherwise eligible to participate in the program but is not a member of a retirement plan administered by the Virginia Retirement System the first time he is hired or rehired on or after January 1, 2014, in a covered position, shall participate in the hybrid retirement program established by this section.

rules.title: Check your plan: hazardous duty benefits equal to the State Police Officers' Retirement System's. Your normal retirement date is your 60th birthday

source.quote: "Normal retirement date" means a member's sixtieth birthday.

rules.title: Ask your employer whether it provides the enhanced hazardous duty benefits (a political subdivision elects them by resolution approved by the Board)

source.quote: By resolution legally adopted and approved by the Board, the employer may elect to provide benefits equivalent to those provided under the State Police Officers' Retirement System

tables.question: When can I retire, with an unreduced or a reduced benefit?

rules.title: Service retirement: not yet eligible (Plan 1 needs age 55 with 5 years (reduced), age 50 with 10 years (50/10), age 50 with 30 years or age 65 with 5 years (unreduced))

source.quote: Any member in service who has attained his fifty-fifth birthday with five or more years of creditable service may retire prior to his normal retirement date upon written notification to the Board setting forth the date the retirement is to become effective.

rules.title: Check reduced early retirement: you may retire now with an allowance reduced for each year before your unreduced date (Plan 1: age 50 with 10 or more years (the 50/10 allowance))

source.quote: Any member in service on or after January 1, 1994, who has attained his fiftieth birthday with 10 or more years of creditable service may retire prior to his normal retirement date upon written notification to the Board setting forth the date the retirement is to become effective.

tables.question: What should I do about service credit, contributions and beneficiaries?

rules.title: Check whether to buy service credit for prior public service, certain leaves, or up to four years of active duty military service

fee.rule: the approximate normal cost within 24 months of hire or of the leave's end; the actuarial equivalent cost after that

source.quote: any member in service may purchase up to four years of service credit for prior active duty military service in the armed forces of the United States

rules.deadline: within the first 24 months of active service after hire (or after the leave ends) to pay the approximate normal cost; later purchases cost the actuarial equivalent

deadline_source.quote: If the member does not purchase, or enter into a purchase of service credit contract for, the service made available in this subsection within the first 24 months of the member's active service following his first date of hire or the final day of any applicable leave of absence, as applicable, then, for each year or portion thereof to be credited at the time of purchase, the member shall pay the actuarial equivalent cost.

rules.title: Keep your contributions in VRS if you leave: with five or more years of service you can retire later (deferred retirement)

source.quote: Any member who terminates service after five or more years of creditable service, regardless of termination date, may retire under the provisions of subsection A, B, or D if he has not withdrawn his accumulated contributions

rules.title: Plan the hybrid plan's defined contribution part: your employer contributes 1% of pay and matches your voluntary contributions

source.quote: The employer shall make a mandatory contribution to the defined contribution component of the program on behalf of an employee participating in the program in the amount of one percent of creditable compensation

rules.title: Tell VRS whom you designate as your beneficiary if you die before retirement

source.quote: Each member shall designate who is to receive a refund of accumulated contributions credited to his account in the event of the death of the member prior to retirement.

tables.question: What if I become disabled or die before I retire?

rules.title: Check disability retirement if a disability stops you working (in service, or within 90 days after leaving, with your contributions still in VRS)

source.quote: Any member in service or within ninety days after termination of service who has not withdrawn his accumulated contributions as provided for in § 51.1-128 may retire for disability

rules.title: Tell your family: if you die in service, a retirement allowance is paid to a designated surviving spouse, minor child or parent

source.quote: a retirement allowance shall be paid to the person or persons designated as provided in subsection A of this section if the person is the member's (i) surviving spouse, (ii) minor child, or (iii) parent(s).

assumptions.text: The Social Security retirement age (Plan 2 and Hybrid normal retirement date) is taken as 67, the age for people born in 1960 or later.
assumptions.direction: overstates the age for members born before 1960 (66 to 66 and 10 months), who reach the unreduced date earlier

assumptions.text: Age and creditable service are whole years; creditable service includes purchased service and excludes refunded service.
assumptions.direction: a member a few months short of a threshold is shown as not yet eligible

assumptions.text: Hybrid plan members are 'persons who become members on or after July 1, 2010' for § 51.1-153, so the Plan 2 eligibility rules apply to their defined benefit.
assumptions.direction: none expected: the hybrid program's defined benefit follows Plan 2

assumptions.text: Hazardous duty means benefits equal to the State Police Officers' Retirement System's: a state police officer, a VaLORS member under § 51.1-216, or a political subdivision employee whose employer elected § 51.1-138 benefits.
assumptions.direction: VaLORS members hired before 1 July 2001 who did not elect, and employers that did not elect, follow the general Plan 1 or Plan 2 rules instead

assumptions.text: The 2014 window in which Plan 1 and Plan 2 members could elect the hybrid program (§ 51.1-169(A)), and § 51.1-153(B)(4) resolutions treating a subdivision's firefighters, EMS personnel and law-enforcement officers as Plan 1, are not modelled.
assumptions.direction: a member who elected the hybrid plan, or is covered by such a resolution, gets the wrong plan here
